I was quoted €434 for a simple x-ray on my dog, along with other services I hadn't requested. Naturally, I refused the quote.

Despite this, I was charged €63 for a "visit." Visit for what, exactly? The dog was simply manipulated a little around the sides, without the exam I had come for.

I find it absurd to have to pay €63 for a service that, in my opinion, achieved nothing, after having already received a quote of €434 for an x-ray.

I felt more like I was dealing with a cash-generating machine than a facility truly interested in the needs of the patient and the owner.

Highly discouraged. Stay away. Never again!

Unfortunately, my experience was very negative. I took my Toy Poodle for a simple grooming session and found his fur cut very short, and, more importantly, very uneven and unkempt. The end result was far from what I expected, and my dog ​​looked completely different.
I'm especially disappointed because I expected more attention and professionalism, considering the delicate nature and characteristics of a Toy Poodle's coat. Before entrusting my dog ​​to this groomer again, I would definitely think twice.

We entered the clinic at opening time to request an appointment for our dog, but no one greeted us. The waiting room was empty, and there was no staff at the desk. We could clearly hear the presence of a dog and someone inside, but no one came to ask us why we were there, or even to simply tell us to wait a few minutes. After about 20 minutes of waiting, we left. Fortunately, our dog wasn't in an emergency, but it's natural to wonder what would have happened if it had been an emergency. A little attention and communication would have made all the difference.

Good morning, I unfortunately have to report a bad experience with Cyclina Veterinaria.
We found them to be unprofessional, inexperienced, and just obsessed with billing. I DO NOT RECOMMEND THEM.

I have a dog and we take out a health plan for her every year. Whenever something isn't right, I stop by and they're always kind and helpful. Plus, the plan, which I can pay monthly, includes all my little girl's vaccinations and exams.

It's a bit like a dentist, but for furry friends, and the prices are in line.

I went yesterday for an ultrasound on my golden retriever puppy, and upon arrival, the anesthesiologist and radiographer were already waiting for us at the reception. They were kind and welcoming. Furthermore, the explanation of the results was clear, and they even recommended a ligament supplement specifically for puppies, which can be purchased both on-site and at the pharmacy (so no pressure to pay extra right away), something our local vet never bothered to suggest in a month. Excellent point of reference!

It took me a couple of years to write this review, which, thanks to my less-than-positive experience with Cà Zampa Portello, I learned to do.
I believe I was among Cà Zampa Portello's first customers; the completely new style intrigued me, and I was looking for a facility close to home for my big dog.
A nice, convenient idea (close to home), with extended opening hours, including weekends. I found an excellent veterinarian, which makes up for the somewhat steep costs. However, I've noticed a certain decline in the overall organization, which seems too focused on financial gain to the detriment of overall professionalism, quality of care, and customer service. Since veterinary medicine is ALL the responsibility of the pet owner (even though we call ourselves parents), we expect that same professionalism from everyone: the MedVet who treats my dog ​​is unquestionable, but the rest of the practice is questionable. Here are some points that deserve attention:
1) Ultrasound doctor replaced at the last minute WITHOUT informing the client (who had booked an appointment with another doctor); the replacement doctor was unfamiliar with the case, and the client was forced to explain the dog's medical history to the new doctor; the exam was performed extremely quickly; the report was incomplete and superficial (perhaps copied and pasted from someone else) and unsigned. NO ADMINISTRATIVE PERSON CANNOT AND MUST NOT AFFORD TO REPLACE A DOCTOR WITHOUT CLEARLY INFORMING THE CLIENT, WHO RESERVES THE RIGHT TO CANCEL THE EXAM/VISIT OR REQUEST A NEW APPOINTMENT. The reception staff was in excessive haste in demanding payment.
2) Blood sample lost in the lab (hoping it arrived at the lab, since it has to travel from Milan to Padua; perhaps there are no veterinary laboratories in our city?); Not all urine tests are performed (we're talking about basic tests);
3) The owner MUST always request the test reports, otherwise weeks pass waiting. Even the worst public facility sets a date for the collection of reports that it commits to respect.
4) Lack of veterinary technicians who can assist the MedVet in performing procedures, such as holding the dog while the sample is taken. The client isn't always able to do this correctly. Perhaps these technicians are available, but they always perform a secretarial/administrative role that makes it impossible to request their support.
5) When the MedVet treating my dog ​​changed his hours of availability at the clinic, NO ONE from management bothered to inform me. When I asked the then-Director for an explanation, the response was, "There are so many of you, I certainly can't call everyone." So what is she doing here? Just counting the day's income?
If you want to maintain the style you started with, review your internal organization as soon as possible. These days, it's not that difficult to communicate dissatisfaction through social media and word of mouth.
In the end, I decided to change Veterinary Clinics. There's certainly no shortage of options in Milan, and it's not difficult to find a good, better-organized facility that's more respectful of its clients, and even cheaper and better organized.
Oh, I also changed my Grooming Service... I'm waiting for the options in the city for those, too!
